findings.impact: A failing test included in the ordinary full Go workflow can be skipped while the report and receipt claim passing validation.
findings.text: In src/test-impact/verification.ts:193, preflight uses --untracked-files=no, while actualInventory records only Go package directories and discoverComparison reads only committed blobs. An untracked Go test in an existing, otherwise unaffected package is therefore neither a dirty mismatch nor a discovery change. Reproduced with a full passing baseline for packages a and b, a commit changing only a, then untracked b/untracked_test.go containing t.Fatal: verify reports checkout.dirty=false, selects only ./a, and creates a validated receipt; go test ./... fails in b. Catch relevant untracked or ignored runner inputs at the initial checkout observation and broaden or fail appropriately, without introducing mid-run mutation proof. Consider source files and other Go-discovered resources, including ignored inputs.

findings.impact: An analyzer finding of an affected test can be dropped, so the runner may certify a subset that omits a test the Trail-code graph says must run.
findings.text: In src/test-impact/verification.ts:235-236 the analyzer's affected paths are used only to check that they include independent discoveries; the final selection at the selective branch uses discovered.affected and fallback scopes, never the analyzer's additional affected units. Reproduced by adding b/b_test.go to an otherwise valid v2 affected array through the existing post-analysis test seam: the report is accepted, runs only ./a, and creates a validated receipt while ./b is omitted. Map all analyzer-reported affected test units and dependents into final scope, or fail closed if a reported path or relation cannot be mapped; reject malformed affected entries instead of silently filtering them.

findings.impact: The frozen suite permits both observed false-validation paths to regress unnoticed.
findings.text: Add real Go regression coverage for an untracked failing test in an unchanged existing package after establishing the baseline, and assert verification cannot selectively validate while go test ./... fails. Include a relevant ignored source/resource case. Also corrupt an otherwise valid analyzer report to add an affected test unit and assert it is included or forces fallback; assert malformed affected entries cannot justify narrowing. The existing baseline/selection tests only use clean committed checkouts and do not assert preservation of extra analyzer results.

spec: Implement the shared deterministic helper and a real repository adapter per docs/test-impact/design.md sections 2–5, 7–10 and 13–14. Require explicit exact endpoints and use a practical target preflight and the normal test-runner stable-input assumption. Discover and map actual runner targets, include changed tests, apply declared invalidation and full fallback rules, preserve original full workflows and gates, report separate impact, plan, execution and verification statuses, and implement compatible baseline receipts and receipt chaining. Missing or incompatible baseline expands execution to the full configured profile. Include meaningful acceptance tests for the snapshot, discovery, fallback, evidence, error and execution contracts. Select a representative project and runner through design; no model invocation in normal runs. The full design is binding. Work directly in this fork for an eventual upstream pull request; no separate product repository or subtree. Owner scope clarification: Initial release requires explicit committed Git endpoints only, and must work across platforms and filesystems with ordinary Git repositories, without Btrfs, privileged operations, special mounts or subvolumes. Worktree target support is deferred; reject it clearly rather than silently substituting a commit. Use ordinary test-runner execution with a stable-input assumption and a practical target preflight; do not require proof of checkout immutability, mutation monitoring, filesystem snapshots, or isolated checkout. Adapt the original worktree-specific acceptance cases accordingly.
